passage:
A fruit stand near the bus stop sells bananas, apples, and oranges. The owner, Mrs. Lin, always places a small basket on the side. The sign says, "Ugly fruit, half price."
The fruit in the basket may have strange shapes or small marks, but it is still good to eat. At first, people did not buy it. They thought ugly fruit must taste bad.
One day, Mrs. Lin cut an ugly apple into pieces and let customers try it. It was sweet and fresh. After that, the basket became popular.
Mrs. Lin says people and fruit are sometimes judged too quickly by appearance. A mark on the outside does not always tell the truth about what is inside.
